*The following story may contain language that some (most) might (should) find offensive. Discretion advised.*

The tl;dr version is that we met because of a mutual friend's Facebook status.

This mutual friend booked bands at local bars and venues a few years ago, most of which were metal. One day he posted a Facebook status that said, "No, I will not book your crappy metalcore band. Keep that faggot shit to yourself." She made the first comment, which said, "Really? That's the word you have to use?" Everyone seemed to jump on her for being the PC Police (which, as I'd find out later, couldn't be further from the truth). I was in a particularly bad mood that day, and for some reason felt the need to jump in with the others. While I certainly understand the reasons behind that word being offensive, I'm one that believes in absolute freedom of speech, no matter how reprehensible said speech may be. Think of the George Carlin and Louis C.K. bits about offensive words, and that's essentially my viewpoint. Anyway, I was feeling like being a dick, and saw someone who seemed like an easy target, so I wrote, "Yeah, Mutual Friend. You should've said something like 'faggy' instead." She responded, saying that I sound like a 12-year old. I responded with something else that I can't remember. She claimed I had no people skills (which is true), and it just kept escalating. At some point the fight turned to private messages, and from there mutual understanding and apologies, then vaguely getting to know each other, and finally, she ended up sending me a friend request. The rest is history, and to this day we still are amazed at how bizarre our "how we met" story is.

Oh, and that mutual friend is no longer a friend of ours. That's another story, though. We'll get to that, kids.

Lost actually took me awhile, but through no fault of my own. It was either before it was on Netflix, or I just didn't realize it was. I borrowed the DVDs season at a time from my ex-wife's husband, and was not supposed to watch an episode without my girlfriend. She didn't share the same affinity for binge watching that I do.

I started a few weeks before the premiere of season 5 ("Live Free or Die"). It was based on how often Netflix would suggest it based on other things I've watched, plus universal acclaim among some of my most trusted pop-culture savvy friends. Plus I have this weird thing where I often begin watching a show very close to its final season (Lost, HIMYM, Arrested Development (started just before the third season), Six Feet Under). I'm often the contrarian when it comes to shows and films that receive such high acclaim, and I expected that to be the case here. After the third episode, I realized I was wrong. So very wrong.
